# Halloran Press Shop Handbook

## Pressroom practice

- The Halloran press is inked before the first sheet each morning with exactly 30 grams of black ink, worked out on the stone with the palette knife for five minutes until the whole disc is an even satin with no streaks. The printer who inks the press initials the shop card, and an ink fountain topped up by anyone else is wiped and begun again, since a mixed ink dries unevenly and leaves a ghost on the back of the sheet that the customer sees under a window. The knife is cleaned with paraffin rag after use, and the rag goes straight into the red tin with the lid, never into the open bin where a warm morning has set one alight.
- Damp paper goes through the press at a pressure of 12 on the impression dial, and the dial is set by the head printer at the start of the shift and sealed with a dab of wax so that nobody wanders it in the course of the day. If the paper arrives dry from the store the printer damps it at the trough and leaves it under a board for at least four hours to take the water evenly. A sheet printed too wet cockles on the drying line; a sheet printed too dry shows the grain of the felt, and the whole run of three hundred must then be re-fed through the press, which costs a day.
- Type is distributed back into the case on the same day it is used, and any sort that has been dropped on the floor is thrown in the melting pot rather than returned to the case because a bent sort will print a hairline slur that proof readers find only after a thousand copies are done. The compositor reads each forme backwards against the copy before locking up, and calls the head printer to read it again if the job is for the council, whose notices carry a penalty clause for each misprint. Spaces and quads are counted into their boxes at the end of the week.
- The platen is cleaned every Friday at 3 o'clock, and the stop for the cleaning is signalled by the shop bell so every hand stops together. The platen is wiped with spirit and a lint-free cloth and polished with a few drops of oil on a fresh cloth, never on the platen itself, because oil on the face smears the next morning's first sheet. The head printer inspects the platen under the lamp with the apprentices watching, and scratches or pitting are reported at once to the foundry man, who comes on Mondays.
- Paper stock is counted into the loft ledger every month by the apprentice, and the figure is compared with the delivery book by the head printer who signs for it. A shortage of more than one ream between the ledger and the book is investigated before any new paper is ordered, since the loft key is shared by four people and the paper merchant's invoices are always disputed when the loft count is not clean. Spoilage sheets are kept in the waste loft until the end of the quarter, when the rag man buys them by weight.
